**Bottom line:** the in-repo code (Features #7-#9 and the server around them) is built, tested, containerised, and the

| A/B data file: one writer, optional fsync, growth warning | **verified locally**: 19 unit tests (live holder refused at once, crashed holder taken over, abandoned or unverifiable locks, writes refused once the lock is lost, fsync on and off, growth warning); `scripts/smoke.sh` with real processes (clean exit releases the lock, a second process is refused, SIGTERM releases it, a SIGKILLed holder is taken over with its data intact); `scripts/probe-image.sh` run against a stubbed `docker`, and it fails when the lock is disabled. **Real-container probe: first CI run (`aee583f`) failed in the probe script, not the server.** The hard-killed container with `AB_FSYNC=1` was recovered and the second container was refused with the right message after waiting about 17 s, but `docker logs | grep -q` under `pipefail` returned SIGPIPE (141) and reported a wrong reason. Fixed by capturing output before matching; a config test now forbids `| grep -q` in pipefail scripts. **Re-run on `ce5d7d9` ([run 37392529986](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/actions/runs/37392529986)): all five jobs green; the real-daemon probe ran every section and printed `probe: OK`, with the `[lock]` section taking 17.3 s (the designed wait before a second container on another hostname is refused).** The replacement-pod-after-a-hard-kill path is therefore now exercised on a real daemon too (the `[persistence]` section took about 14 s, waiting out the dead container's lock). The foreign-hostname path (a replacement pod after a hard kill waits up to about 15 s) is covered by planted-lock unit tests and by the real-container probe | PR #10, merged as `00fdefe`; its real-container probe also passed on `main` run 37393158999 |
| HTTP hardening: crash on a bad tool input, shutdown, timeouts, open-server refusal, optional rate limit | **verified locally** (PR #11): a `discover_apis` call with a non-string `query` killed the whole server in HTTP and stdio mode (reproduced, exit 1); a stalled client held the process through SIGTERM (still running 8 s later; Node's default request timeout is 300 s) and `/ready` refused connections instead of answering 503; Node's header and request timeouts were 60 s and 300 s; an empty `AUTH_TOKEN` on `HOST=0.0.0.0` silently turned authentication off. Fixed at the root and with last-resort catches in both transports, a drain then deadline shutdown, explicit 10 s and 30 s receive timeouts, a refusal to start open beyond loopback (`ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=1` to override) and an optional global token-bucket limit (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`, off). Unit tests for each (every one fails when its fix is removed), `scripts/smoke.sh` with real processes and `scripts/probe-image.sh` extended for the real image (stub run passes, each new check fails when its fix is removed). **Real-image probe on a real Docker daemon: passed on the first CI run** ([run 37396176911](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/actions/runs/37396176911), head `5def8d4`, all five jobs green). Its log shows every section ran, including `[exposure]` (the image without a token refuses to start) and `[shutdown]` (`docker stop` exited 0 and left no lock file), ending in `probe: OK`. **NOT VERIFIED:** any real cluster (drain time against a real load balancer, keep-alive against its idle timeout). ## What has been done

1. **Starting point:** three MCP modules, five vendored third-party submodules and a lot of documentation. The earlier
   "production-ready, verified savings, approved" reports were not true: the tests only checked hardcoded fixtures and the
   sign-offs, load tests and scans never happened.
2. **[PR #2](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/2), audit and critical fixes:** working build; a runnable server (stdio and HTTP with
   health, metrics and auth); a real Welch t-test replacing hardcoded A/B statistics; routing and gateway bug fixes; real
   tests for the three modules; Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests and CI rewritten to match the code; fabricated documents
   removed; the missing Headroom submodule added.
3. **[PR #3](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/3), A/B persistence:** append-only log (`AB_DATA_FILE`) with crash recovery, a persistent volume in Kubernetes.
4. **[PR #4](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/4), image verification:** CI pulls the pushed image back by digest and probes that copy.
5. **[PR #5](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/5), private-image deployment:** optional `ghcr-pull` secret and a deployment runbook.
6. **[PR #6](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/6), this roadmap.**
7. **[PR #7](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/7), Windows-friendly local verification:** a cross-platform `build` clean step (`rm -rf` does not exist in `cmd.exe`), `.gitattributes` forcing LF line endings (CRLF breaks the shell scripts and some config tests), and one POSIX-permission test assertion skipped on Windows. Not yet run on a real Windows machine.
8. **[PR #8](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/8), runtime upgrade:** Node 20 (end-of-life) to Node 24 LTS in the Dockerfile and CI, `@types/node` 24, `engines` `>=22`, and a test that keeps one Node major across the image stages, every CI step and `@types/node`.

9. **[PR #9](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/9), SBOM and dependency updates:** CycloneDX SBOM of the production npm tree generated and validated in CI, an SBOM attestation attached to the pushed image, and a Dependabot config for npm, GitHub Actions and Docker.
10. **[PR #10](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/10), A/B data file safety:** a lock file makes the data file single-writer (second process refused, crashed holder's lock taken over, writes fail closed if the lock is lost), `AB_FSYNC=1` flushes every append, a warning at `AB_DATA_WARN_BYTES` (default 100 MB), SIGTERM/SIGINT handling in stdio mode so the lock is released. Compaction was **not** built: nothing can be deleted today, so it would only drop corrupt lines; real size control needs a rollup design (open decision). Merged as `00fdefe`; the real-container probe passed on a real Docker daemon, first failing on a bug in the probe script itself (`grep -q` under `pipefail` returned SIGPIPE), which is fixed and guarded by a test.
11. **[PR #11](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/11), HTTP hardening (roadmap step 5):** a tool or handler that throws can no longer end the process (one `discover_apis` call could); graceful shutdown (`/ready` 503 while draining, a hard deadline so a stalled client cannot hold the process); explicit receive timeouts; the server refuses to start on a non-loopback `HOST` without `AUTH_TOKEN`; an optional global rate limit, **off by default** because no load test has measured a safe number. Merged as `4758195`; the real-daemon probe passed (the new exposure and shutdown sections ran), and so did the `main` run, including the copy pulled back from GHCR.
12. **[PR #12](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/12), latency metrics and alert-rule validation (roadmap step 6):** a tool-call latency histogram, a counter for refused (401) requests, a latency alert (provisional threshold), `promtool check rules` and `promtool test rules` over every alert (`scripts/check-prometheus.sh`, `monitoring/alerts.test.yaml`) and a CI job that builds promtool from a pinned, checksum-verified Prometheus release (`scripts/install-promtool.sh`). Merged as `2acb01b`; its CI run passed, including the new `prometheus` job (promtool built in 2 min 14 s to 2 min 37 s on the runner) and the real-daemon probe.
13. **[PR #13](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/13), handoff file and changelog (roadmap step 7):** `CLAUDE.md` (stable context and working rules for future sessions) and `CHANGELOG.md` (everything under *Unreleased*, behaviour changes flagged), with tests that fail when the handoff file names an environment variable, script, file or CI job that does not exist, when the code reads a variable it does not name, or when the changelog misses a pull request listed here. Merged as `a41d48a`.
14. **[PR #14](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/14), measured baselines (roadmap step 8):** `scripts/loadtest.js` (closed and open loop, per tool, server-side means) and `scripts/capacity.js` (A/B data size against restart, memory and query cost), their results and what they mean in `PERFORMANCE.md`, and one safe configuration correction found by the measurements: the manifests set `AB_DATA_WARN_BYTES` to 16 MiB, because the A/B module holds every measurement in memory (about 500 bytes each) and reaches the manifests' 256Mi limit near 360 000 measurements (a 41 MiB file; corrected in PR #15: roughly 400 000 to 460 000), long before the 100 MiB default warning. Step 9 (PR #15) undid the 16 MiB warning: the memory no longer grows.
15. **[PR #15](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/15), A/B memory and query cost (roadmap step 9):** the A/B module keeps counts and a running mean and variance per variant and metric instead of every measurement, and replays the data file in chunks; the file itself is unchanged, so nothing is lost. Held to the previous implementation by a golden-master test (120 datasets whose answers came from the old code, replayed at several read sizes), a differential run of 5 020 random experiments (1 differs in a rounded last digit, on data near 1 000 000 000) and a differential run on 3 000 randomly damaged data files (torn tails, blank lines, CRLF, invalid UTF-8; log lines and state identical, apart from 16 files of identical constants where the old code printed floating-point noise and the new one the exact answer, and 1 rounding digit). Memory regression checks that fail on the previous code: `scripts/smoke.sh` replays 400 000 measurements under a 48 MiB heap (the old code died with "heap out of memory" even at 96 MiB) and the container probe starts the image on 500 000 measurements inside `--memory=256m`. Two small fixes found on the way: a measurement without a `metrics` object no longer breaks every later results call, and identical constant series compare as equal. `AB_DATA_WARN_BYTES` in the manifests goes back to 100 MiB. Docs corrected: an empty server idles at 62 MiB, not 85. CI on the PR head `5b7afa5` ([run 37417671122](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/actions/runs/37417671122)): all six jobs green, logs read: 184 tests passed, smoke including `[memory]` ending `smoke: OK`, promtool `SUCCESS`, and all eight probe sections of the real-daemon run including the new `[capacity]` (`probe: OK`).
16. **[PR #16](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/16), startup probe (roadmap step 10):** replay time measured at one core (about 10 s for 8 000 000 measurements) and at about half a core (about 20 s, 2.6 microseconds each; the CPU limit emulated by sharing a core with an equal-priority busy loop, which halved a pure CPU loop), so a full 1Gi volume takes about 23 s at the limit against a liveness window of about 35 s. Both manifests gain a `startupProbe` (180 s); a config test ties its window to the volume size and the CPU limit (5 of 5 mutations caught). Not applied to a cluster.
17. **[PR #17](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/17), event-loop delay metric (roadmap step 11):** `increadible_event_loop_delay_seconds` (a histogram of how late a 10 ms timer ran) and the `IncreadibleEventLoopBlocked` alert (a tick more than 1 s late in 5 minutes). Why this and not a per-request duration histogram: the capacity test showed `/health` taking seconds during query bursts while the tool histogram showed milliseconds, because a handler starts only after the loop is free; only a loop-level timer sees the block. Native `monitorEventLoopDelay` was rejected after an experiment (it records the whole interval and drops the first sample after each reset, which is the one a block lands in). Guards: 4 unit tests (5 of 5 mutations caught after one gap was found and closed), smoke and the container probe freeze the process for 1.3 s (`SIGSTOP`, `docker pause`) and require the late tick (4 of 4 controls on the checks themselves: monitor not started, monitor reporting zero, no stall, probe without the pause), 2 promtool cases (4 of 4 valid mutations of the rule caught; the first draft of the rule matched nothing, because `_count` has no `le` label, and its own firing case exposed that). No measurable overhead (18 142 and 18 211 against 18 680 and 17 865 requests per second). Merged as `15b2c83`; its `main` run is in the snapshot above.
18. **[PR #18](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/18), `AB_FSYNC` on in the manifests (owner decision, 2026-10-07):** both manifests set `AB_FSYNC=1`, so an acknowledged A/B write survives a node crash or power loss. Measured earlier at about 0.2 ms per write on a local disk (ceiling about 3 500 writes per second); **NOT VERIFIED on the cluster's storage class**. The value is checked against the code's own parser (a value such as `on` would be read as off): 4 of 4 mutations caught (production value `on`, staging variable missing, parser dropping `yes`, a looser parser). The image and the code still default to off.
19. **[PR #19](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/19), A/B metric semantics (roadmap step 12, first half of multi-variant/multi-metric):** `direction` per metric, `primary_metric` per experiment, and `guardrail` metrics that can withhold a winner. Found while reading the winner rule: the first metric always decided and the higher mean always won, so a significantly *cheaper* variant was reported as the loser, which is the wrong answer for a cost-routing product. Old experiments answer exactly as before (the 120-dataset golden master is unchanged); 24 new tests including a negate-and-flip symmetry test on 40 random datasets; 12 of 12 deliberate breakages caught (one of my mutations did not compile, which proved nothing, and was redone). A guardrail with no data withholds the winner (fail closed). More than two variants is the second half, in the next PR.
20. **[PR #20](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/20), A/B with two to ten variants (roadmap step 12, second half):** equal or weighted traffic; a variant wins only if it is significantly better than every other one, with Holm's correction over all pairs of variants on the primary metric (three variants at p about 0.03 each: a winner against one rival, none against two, tested); every pair reported in `comparisons`. Two-variant experiments are unchanged: sticky assignments checked against a fixture recorded from the previous implementation (27 cases, 409 users) and the 120-dataset golden master byte-identical. 26 new tests, 20 of 20 deliberate breakages caught (my first run of the controls reported all 20 as "not caught" because of a bug in my own driver, and also showed one real gap, the confidence rule, which a new test now covers).
21. **[PR #21](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/21), API gateway live mode (roadmap step 13):** `call_api` can make real GET requests, opt-in per API (`GATEWAY_LIVE_APIS`; the default is unchanged: mock data, no network, and every result now says `source`). The work is mostly security: `endpoint` and `params` come from a model, so they cannot reach another host or path (URL, `//`, `..`, encoded dots or slashes, `?`, `#`, backslashes, control characters all refused; a 60 000-endpoint property test holds), cannot set or override the credential, redirects are never followed, only JSON is accepted, time and size are capped, and a credential never appears in a result, error (an error body that repeats it is scrubbed), log line or cache key. Found while testing: a bare `/` on an API whose registered URL is the whole endpoint (Wikipedia's `/w/api.php`) would have produced `/w/api.php/`; fixed. 88 tests against a real local HTTP server plus the built-in registry's credential placement (mocked `fetch`); 29 of 30 deliberate breakages caught and the 30th shown redundant (a second layer behind three others, with the property test passing without it); the first control run also exposed two real test gaps (the inner credential scrubbing was masked by an outer one; error-body length was untested), now covered. **Not tried against any real provider** (the sandbox cannot reach them).

From its pinned 7.3.0 source (not run; the published package was already 7.4.1): a plain install does not change the machine but its installer writes hooks into the global Claude settings, and its telemetry is opt-in. `agentacct`: the owner's condition was *proven, running in the market now, one of its kind*; on the evidence it is an early-alpha project about ten weeks old (766 stars) and far from unique (ccusage has 18.9k stars and 18 agents; provider billing is the ground truth), so it is **not** used. Real savings are to be measured with this server's A/B module (cost primary and `lower_is_better`, quality as guardrail) on a real workload: **BLOCKED** on a workload and a quality score.
23. **[PR #23](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/23), audit of the whole repository, part 1: API gateway resource bounds (findings GW-1, GW-3, GW-4):** found by probing the built server, not by reading alone. The result cache was unbounded (2 000 distinct calls with 200 KB of params = 385 MB of heap, over the 256Mi limit) and `aggregate_apis` started every call it was given at once (5 000 requested, 5 000 started together). Now: at most 500 cache entries and about 16 MiB, at most 10 live calls at once with 100 waiting, at most 100 calls per aggregate run five at a time, and a call that fails no longer discards the others (**behaviour change**, flagged in `CHANGELOG.md`). Evidence: 17 new tests; 21 deliberate breakages caught (one check shown redundant and removed); Node 24 and Node 22 clean rooms. The whole audit is reported in [`AUDIT.md`](AUDIT.md).
24. **[PR #24](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/24), audit part 2: A/B inputs and the interval for few values (findings AB-2 to AB-7):** probing found that one finite `1.7e308` permanently spoils an experiment, that duplicate or missing variant ids and misspelt metric ids were accepted, that `null`/array metrics and an object `user_id` were stored, and that the 95% interval of a metric with few values used a t shortcut that is too narrow (df 1: 4.33 against 12.71). Fixed for new writes only (stored data still loads). The p-value approximation was checked against an independent exact t distribution and is conservative below 25 degrees of freedom (no change). The golden master changed in one deliberate, independently checked way: 58 `ci_95` numbers in 13 of 120 datasets, nothing else. Evidence: 13 new tests plus a rewritten one; 21 deliberate breakages caught (including a typo in one of the 29 table entries that only an independent oracle in the test could see).
25. **[PR #25](https://github.com/nitro0dust-pixel/Increadible/pull/25), audit part 3: routing state and protocol conformance (findings RT-1 to RT-5, P-1 to P-6):** probing showed that `update_rules` changed the live rules before writing the file (a failed write, such as the read-only ConfigMap in the manifests, left routing changed after reporting an error), that a rule id like `constructor` corrupted the stats (`NaN%`), that a rules file which parsed but held a malformed rule broke every routing call, and that the transports accepted `jsonrpc: "1.0"`, object ids, any `protocolVersion`, answered notifications, and refused `HEAD /health`, `/health?x=1` and a lower-case `bearer` with 401. Fixed; one validator now serves both `update_rules` and the rules file at startup. Evidence: 64 new tests; the new tests fail against the old files (27 of 35 routing tests, 13 and 5 protocol tests); 29 deliberate breakages caught, one redundant check removed.

D-2 the workflow cancelled any running CI run on a newer push, `main` included, so two quick merges would cancel the first merge's image push and verification by digest; `main` runs are no longer cancelled (config test). D-3 `scripts/verify.sh` wrote its log to one fixed `/tmp` path, printed nothing about which tree it tested, passed when jest ran fewer suites than there are test files (the way a stale checkout had reported 189 of 195 tests) and said nothing at all about the alert-rule check; it now names the commit and whether the tree was clean, fails a partial run, uses a unique log, and reports the alert-rule check or `NOT AVAILABLE`. D-4 there was no tracked way to test exactly what is committed (the discrepancy investigation used an untracked script that archived the wrong tree): `scripts/cleanroom.sh [commit]`. Both scripts are run for real against stubs and a throwaway git repository (`tests/scripts.test.ts`, 15 tests; 20 deliberate breakages caught, 1 shown equivalent; the first run of the control left `set -e` untested, which an added test now covers). **Recorded, not changed (owner decisions):** D-5 the secret scanner's action is pinned (`trufflehog@v3.97.9`) but the scanner itself is not: the log of run 37709478593 shows `VERSION: latest` and `trufflehog_version 3.99.0` (image digest `sha256:39ee0643...`); D-6 the `docker` job does not wait for the `prometheus` job, so a push to `main` with broken alert rules would still publish an image (the image holds no alert rules). The stale test and coverage figures in this file (334 tests, 93.1%) were corrected from the CI log. ## Backlog (unscheduled)

- **Release process:** the procedure is `docs/RELEASING.md` (who tags, which commit, the package's SHA-256 checked from two builds; since PR #70 the tag step checks the remote, the commit, the push and the tag on GitHub). Released: `v1.0.2` (2026-10-09), `v1.0.3` (2026-10-10), `v1.0.4` (2026-10-14), and **`v1.0.5` (2026-10-29, tagged on `61ff561` with a GitHub Release page and `increadible-1.0.5.mcpb` attached; upgraded in the owner's Claude Desktop with `User-Agent contact: set` verified)**.
- **Handoff:** `CLAUDE.md` holds the stable context and working rules for future sessions; the status stays here.
- **Request drivers (`docs/DRIVERS.md`):** **stages 1 to 4 done** (PR #69, PR #75, PR #76, PR #81) and **verified on both Linux and Windows 11 (`Nitro-Dust`, 2026-10-29)**. Stage 2: three scenarios (`gateway`, `ab-statistics`, `routing-rules`) and the scenario format they needed. Stage 3 (PR #76, `docs/DRIVERS-WORKFLOW.md`): `npm run drive:all` (13 of 13 jobs PASS on Linux and Windows 11) and the workflows `drive-gate` and `engineer-loop` (tested with stand-ins for the agents; a run with real agents is NOT VERIFIED). Stage 4 (PR #81): `npm run drive:live` (`scripts/drive-live.js`, `tests/drive-live.test.ts`), testing the compiled gateway against a local stub HTTP provider on `127.0.0.1` across 9 checks (live GET + cache, credentials + redaction, redirect refusal, 503 retry, 429 short `Retry-After` retry, 429 long `Retry-After` cooldown refusal, per-API and default rate limits, timeout without retry + size cap, and Wikimedia production contact refusal), plus opt-in `--live-probes` verified against the four real keyless providers on Windows 11 (`13/13 PASS`).
- **A/B module:** memory and query cost no longer grow with the data (step 9, `PERFORMANCE.md`). What remains: the data file itself is never compacted (the 1Gi volume holds about 8.9 million measurements and startup replay takes about 9 s for 8 million before the port opens, so a rollup or rotation is for when the volume fills; the `startupProbe` that protects a long replay was added in step 10); the primary metric decides the winner and guardrails can withhold it (PR #19), with 2 to 10 variants (PR #20). Not built: non-inferiority margins for guardrails, and sequential testing (a result is a fixed-sample snapshot, so asking for it repeatedly while data arrives and acting on the first significant answer inflates false positives; decide the sample size first, or add a sequential method).
- **Observability:** a tool-call latency histogram exists but there is no baseline, so the latency alert threshold is provisional; no cost metrics; no dashboard; the rules are unit-tested with promtool but never run against a live Prometheus; no HTTP-level (end-to-end) latency metric, no request log.
- **HTTP:** no TLS, per-client rate limit or request logging; the rate limit is global and off by default; keep-alive timeout is Node's 5 s default, unchecked against a real load balancer's idle timeout.
- **Gated catalog (option A):** step 1a done (PR #50: the registry as data with a gate record per API, all nine `candidate`, answers unchanged). Step 1b started (PR #51): a health probe with written success criteria for each of the four keyless APIs (`catalog.ts`, checks in `probes.ts`), `scripts/record-contracts.js` to record one real answer per probe, and `tests/gateway-contracts.test.ts` to replay recordings through the gateway in CI. **The four recordings exist** (PR #58): the owner ran the recorder on their Windows PC on 2026-10-10 (the sandbox cannot reach the providers); all four replay in CI, and their gate records name that contract test (PR #59). What was found about their terms is in `docs/GATEWAY-GATED-CATALOG.md`, sections 10 and 11 (the nine APIs reviewed on 2026-10-12; not a sign-off). Still open for 1b: the owner's sign-offs (pinned URL, auth class), the terms (read and recorded with a sign-off), then promotion to `gated`; after that `discover_apis` lists gated APIs only, in its own PR. Step 2: a per-API rate limit (PR #52), a default of 5 calls a minute per API, bounded retries with HTTP 429 and Retry-After handled, and Wikimedia's User-Agent rule (PR #63, owner's instruction of 2026-10-12). Step 3: an egress allowlist (PR #53, never applied to a cluster). Step 4 (PR #54): a candidate store of 2,032 entries from the public-apis list (`features/09-api-gateway/data/candidates-public-apis.json`), read by no server code; APIs.guru not imported (unreachable from the sandbox, frozen since 2024-03-01). Which candidates to gate next is the owner's choice; `docs/GATEWAY-CANDIDATES.md` (generated, PR #55) is the material for it, and shows the list calling wikidata `OAuth`, which its read API is not. A probe runner with a probe history exists (PR #66, `scripts/run-probes.js`), never run against the real providers; the retirement threshold is a proposal waiting for the owner.
- **Gateway live mode:** switchable in the Claude Desktop package from 1.0.3 (settings Live APIs and Contact, empty by default; keyless APIs only, no key setting); **verified against the real providers for those four** (one call each from Claude Desktop, 2026-10-10: coingecko `/simple/price`, hackernews `/maxitem.json`, a wikipedia search, a wikidata `wbsearchentities`; `get_api_stats` 4 calls, 4 live, 0 failed); unverified for the key-based APIs and for anything beyond one call each; a per-API rate limiter (`GATEWAY_RATE_LIMITS`, PR #52) with **no per-API value set** (the values wait on each provider's terms) and a default of 5 calls a minute per API (`GATEWAY_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT`, PR #63, the project's own choice); the global `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` stays off; an egress allowlist written but **never applied to a cluster** (the manifests allow DNS only; `k8s/egress-live-cilium.yaml` allows HTTPS to the four keyless providers on Cilium; PR #53); bounded retries after HTTP 429, 502, 503 or 504 or a dropped connection, with backoff and Retry-After (`GATEWAY_RETRIES`, default 1, PR #63); no response schema per provider (it forwards the provider's JSON as is); the nine providers' terms reviewed on 2026-10-12 and signed off by no one (`features/09-api-gateway/data/terms-review.json`).
- **Container hardening:** the secret scanner is pinned by digest (D-5, PR #39); the `docker` job does not wait for the `prometheus` job (D-6, accepted: the image holds no alert rules); no image signing; the image SBOM attestation is unverified; no vulnerability scan; GitHub Actions are pinned by version tag, not by commit SHA.

The `prometheus` CI job builds promtool from source (about 70 seconds from a cold cache on four cores, 2 min 37 s on the GitHub runner, where it is now the longest job); alternatives are a prebuilt image pinned by digest (needs approval to look the digest up) or a build cache (needs a verified `actions/cache` version).

Recommendation: turn it on in the manifests, since A/B writes are rare next to that ceiling and a write that survives a node crash is worth more than 0.2 ms. The image and the code stay off by default; the manifests now turn it on.

## How to keep this file honest

- Every status change cites evidence; "NOT VERIFIED" stays until something has actually been run.
- Projected numbers are never recorded as results.
- Production deployment needs explicit owner approval, recorded here with the date.
